title: Agent-runtime security folds into a hyperscaler-native defense tier by H1 2027
body: The standalone agentic-security category that Straiker's $64M Series A just capitalized will begin collapsing into the platform layer, with at least one major cloud or agent-platform incumbent shipping runtime agent-defense (agent discovery, pre-deployment red-teaming, and behavioral runtime guardrails) as a native, first-party tier by H1 2027. Straiker's three-product framing (Discover, Ascend, Defend) and its claimed 15x run-rate growth prove enterprise demand and a repeatable product shape, while the same-week Claude Cowork sandbox-escape chain shows the agent runtime is a live, disputed vulnerability class the platform owners themselves must answer for. Because the sandbox is the vendor's own containment boundary, the incumbents whose runtimes are being attacked have both the incentive and the telemetry advantage to absorb this defense natively rather than cede it to a pure-play, which compresses the window in which an independent agent-security vendor can stay standalone before it is either acquired or bundled against.

reasoning.because: Straiker's $64M round and a same-week Claude Cowork sandbox escape prove agent-runtime demand
reasoning.given: Platform owners hold the runtime telemetry and containment boundary attackers target
reasoning.so_that: A cloud or agent-platform incumbent ships first-party agent discovery, red-teaming, and runtime guardrails
reasoning.landing: By H1 2027, a major cloud or agent-platform vendor, via ship-or-acquire
reasoning.plain_language: The companies whose AI agents get attacked will build the security in themselves, squeezing the startups now selling it separately.

summary: Straiker's $64M agentic-security round and a same-week Claude Cowork sandbox escape show agent-runtime defense is both funded demand and a live vulnerability. Expect a cloud or agent-platform incumbent to absorb agent discovery, red-teaming, and runtime guardrails into a native tier by H1 2027.
